about.title: San Dimas Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: San Dimas draws visitors and residents alike to its shopping centers along Arrow Highway, its neighborhoods near Bonelli Park, and its downtown Old Town district. Wherever a fall happens, whether it's a wet grocery store floor, a cracked apartment stairwell, or an uneven sidewalk near a local business, property owners in California have a duty to keep conditions reasonably safe. Proving a premises liability claim isn't always straightforward. You generally have to show the owner or manager knew, or should have known, about the hazard and didn't fix it or warn you. That's why documenting what caused your fall and acting quickly to preserve evidence, like surveillance footage that businesses often overwrite within days, matters so much. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves. We simply connect you with an independent attorney in our network who can evaluate what happened and explain your options, free of charge and with no obligation.

whyChoose.title: Why Documentation Matters in a San Dimas Fall Claim

items.title: Proving Notice Takes Evidence
items.desc: California law requires showing the property owner knew or reasonably should have known about the hazard. Photos of the spill, debris, or broken surface right after your fall can be central to establishing that.

items.title: Surveillance Video Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many San Dimas businesses and complexes overwrite security footage within days or weeks. An attorney can send a preservation request quickly, before that footage is gone.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Erase, Your Claim
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, so even if you're found partly responsible for not noticing a hazard, you can still pursue compensation reduced by your share of fault.

items.question: How long do I have to file a premises liability claim in San Dimas?
items.answer: In most cases, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit. If your fall happened on public property, such as a sidewalk maintained by the City of San Dimas or Los Angeles County, that deadline is much shorter and requires an earlier claim process. Because of that difference, it's worth having someone review your situation as soon as possible.

items.question: What if I fell at a shopping center along Arrow Highway or near the SR-57 or SR-210 interchanges?
items.answer: Commercial properties in busy corridors like these often carry insurance and have security systems that may have recorded the area where you fell. An independent attorney can help identify the property owner or manager responsible and request that any footage or incident reports be preserved before they're lost.

items.question: Will it hurt my claim if I was partly at fault for not seeing the hazard?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California follows a pure comparative fault rule, which means you can still recover compensation even if you share some responsibility, though the amount may be reduced by your percentage of fault. An attorney can help evaluate how that might apply to your specific situation.
